thread:
sara_ml: kicked off a focused sweep to compare streaming fanout (SSE/WebSocket) vs bulk non-stream endpoints for v1.4-quant models. collecting p50/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), and GPU utilization across us-west1 and eu-west1 on A100/H100.
jonas_routing: sweet. are you testing multi-client fanout (many small streams) or single large stream?
deepak_quant: both — micro (100 concurrent clients, short sequences) and macro (10 clients, long sequences). quantized int8 and fp16 variants.
ryan_infra: FYI I provisioned identical clusters in both regions and pinned kernel sets: cudnn-89 + custom matmul-optimized kernels on H100, baseline kernels on A100.
benchbot: upload complete: https://redwood.internal/bench/reports/1965432100
sara_ml: quick summary so far — streaming has lower cold-start p50 for short sequences but higher tail (p99) under fanout spikes. non-stream bulk keeps p99 stable but higher median latency for very short reqs.
jonas_routing: that matches intuition: streaming avoids repeated handshake/HTTP overhead, but backpressure across many streams causes p99 spikes when kv-cache thrash kicks in.
deepak_quant: quantization notes: int8 moves throughput up ~1.6x on A100, ~1.9x on H100 for bulk. For streaming the gain is smaller (~1.3x) because token emission and network flushes dominate.
sara_ml: attaching the exact bench commands used:
```
# micro sweep
./bench --model v1.4-int8 --mode streaming --clients 100 --seq 64 --duration 300 --region us-west1 --gpu A100
./bench --model v1.4-int8 --mode nonstream --batch 32 --clients 100 --seq 64 --duration 300 --region us-west1 --gpu A100
```
jonas_routing: can you share the charts? curious about throughput vs p95 overlay.
benchbot: charts uploaded: https://redwood.internal/bench/charts/1965432100/overlay_p95_throughput.png
sara_ml: notable callouts:
- us-west1 H100 streaming p50 ~ 28ms, p95 ~ 220ms (fanout spike), p99 ~ 480ms
- us-west1 H100 nonstream p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 200ms
- eu-west1 A100 shows similar relative trends but absolute throughput is ~10% lower (network + kernel set differences)
ryan_infra: kernel note — on H100 we used matmul-optimizations that reduce per-token op time but increase memory pressure; that explains the larger p99 when many streams share KV cache.
deepak_quant: ops-level: quantized kernels reduce compute but increase memory bandwidth pressure on H100 less efficiently than on A100, so region+GPU combos matter.
jonas_routing: for sizing recommendations: if customers need stable p99 under heavy fanout, prefer non-stream endpoints with batching and higher reserved capacity. If they need low median for interactive short messages, streaming is better but need burst capacity + aggressive cache pinning.
sara_ml: proposed config experiments next:
- streaming + pinned KV (per-client cache) on H100, measure p99
- nonstream low-latency path (small batch=1 + async dispatch) on both GPUs
- mixed routing policy: route short requests to streaming, long to nonstream
ryan_infra: I'll spin the pinned-KV config in us-west1 H100 tomorrow AM. ETA 10:30 PT.
benchbot: scheduled run 1965432115: pinned-kv H100 us-west1
sara_ml: great — let's also capture token-level cost estimates for each curve (tokens/sec * cost/GPU) so product can pick SLAs.
jonas_routing: agree. also add kernel set tag to each chart so we can correlate regressions when kernel upgrades land.
deepak_quant: one more: include eval quality check for int8 vs fp16 on a small prompt set — ensure quant doesn't regress generation quality for the routing policy.
sara_ml: noted. thanks all, will post the pinned-KV run results and a concise recommendation in this thread after the run finishes :thumbsup:
ryan_infra: thanks — will monitor for OOMs during pinned-KV.
benchbot: run complete 1965432199, artifacts: https://redwood.internal/bench/artifacts/1965432100/pinned-kv-results.zip
sara_ml: received, parsing now — will upload a 1-slide TL;DR in ~30m.
